full_narration: Government teams are adopting powerful AI models faster than assurance processes can keep up. Hosted models are the most capable, but using them means sending official information to an outside provider. On-premises models keep data inside the security boundary at the cost of hardware and effort. The brief makes three asks: a central team that scores models on real government tasks, a mandate that every AI-assisted artefact carries a provenance manifest, and funding for a supported offline reference stack. For work touching national security, the default should be fully offline deployment on government hardware, with hosted services allowed only after an explicit data protection assessment. The working group is ready to begin on approval.
